results.title: a house goes offline mid-session
transcript: connected: 7 rooms, stale=false
docker stop threews-ha-1
while down: stale=true status=unreachable rooms=7
docker start threews-ha-1
recovered: 7 rooms, stale=false, no re-subscribe
results.note: The same subscription callback saw the whole sequence. The browser never reloaded and the graph never went empty: it went stale.

results.title: a house flaps up, down, up
transcript: connected through the flap gate; 26 file descriptors held
24 up-down-up cycles at 5000ms; 26 file descriptors held
pool still holds 1 connection(s) for 1 home
breaker opened on attempt 6; subsequent attempts fail in 1ms or less
results.note: No socket leak across the flap, and the breaker turns a connect storm into one fast refusal per call. Warnings are counted, not sampled.

connected with it; 123 entities, 7 rooms

the fleet credential for threews-ha-3 still works: true
results.revoked: 1 of 1 token(s) named "three.ws chaos scenario 3 1788410157622" deleted (listed with auth/refresh_tokens)
results.reacquireMessage: Home Assistant rejected that access token. Create a new long-lived token in your profile and try again.
results.recordedDetail: Home Assistant rejected that access token. Create a new long-lived token in your profile and try again.
results.note: The failure is reported as an auth problem the user can fix by reconnecting, never as an unreachable house, and the connection row records the same thing so the connect screen can explain it without dialling the house again.

results.title: our instance is recycled mid-stream
transcript: established sockets to threews-ha-4 before: 0
while the child streamed: 2
child exited 0 and reported: CLOSED 1
established sockets after: 0
a fresh instance re-subscribed in 30.5ms
results.note: SIGTERM runs the runtime shutdown hook, which closes every held socket. The house sees a clean disconnect rather than a dead connection it has to time out, and the next instance is streaming again in well under a second.

results.title: the database is unavailable
transcript: real store against a dead host: NeonDbError: Error connecting to database: fetch failed
connected with the database up: 7 rooms, readPlan=database
a cold acquire with the database down: Error connecting to database: fetch failed
readPlan is now source=graph rung=degraded_read
with the database down: 7 rooms still readable, write to light.bed_light went through
writePolicy: {"attempt":true,"persistAudit":false}
after the database answers again: readPlan=database
results.realDriverError: NeonDbError: Error connecting to database: fetch failed
results.coldAcquireMessage: Error connecting to database: fetch failed
results.note: Reads degrade to the graph this process already holds, a write is still attempted because a write is somebody pressing a button, and only the audit row waits. A cold acquire fails with a designed error rather than hanging, and the flag clears itself on the first query that answers.

results.title: a slow house, beside a fast one
transcript: a 2000ms delay on every response from threews-ha-7, injected at the socket
fast house alone: p50 1.97ms, p95 6.8ms over 30 calls
slow house at the default 15s connect timeout: connected after 14058ms
slow house connected in 14092ms with a 120s timeout
slow house under load: p50 2005.16ms, p95 2021.04ms
fast house beside it: p50 2.39ms, p95 6.99ms
results.note: Each home has its own socket and its own event loop work; nothing is shared between them but the process. The default 15s connect timeout is what bounds a house this slow in production, and the long timeout here exists only so isolation could be measured with the slow house actually connected.

results.title: a 500 entity house at ten updates a second
transcript: 624 entities, 7 rooms
600 real state changes in 62.1s (9.7/s), 0 failed
61 graph rebuilds: 9.8 updates coalesced into each
graph rebuild p95 0.5ms against a 16.7ms frame budget
heap 17.8MB -> 17.6MB
results.note: The frame budget measured here is the data half: how long it takes to rebuild the room graph the 3D scene renders. Coalescing is what keeps that off the critical path, and the ratio above is it working.
